name: Isolated Segmental Infantile Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Infantile Hemangioma

criteria.description: Hemangioma involving a broad, plaque-like segmental area of skin rather than a focal localized lesion
Appearance of lesion within the first few weeks to months of life
Rapid growth phase during early infancy followed by slow involution
No associated visceral hemangiomas or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of segmental distribution hemangioma with onset in infancy and characteristic proliferative growth phase
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging if needed to exclude deeper involvement

pathognomonic.notes: Distinct large, geographically distributed vascular lesion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapid proliferative growth phase in infancy
pathognomonic.notes: Growth typically peaks by 3-6 months of age
searchTerms: fast growth phase in infant birthmark
quickly growing skin mass in baby
shiny red vascular spot on skin

common.symptomName: Deep bluish or purple subcutaneous component
common.notes: Indicates mixed or deep hemangioma involvement
searchTerms: deep blue or purple lump under skin

common.notes: Common complication especially in segmental lesions

occasional.symptomName: Pain or tenderness at ulcerated sites
Residual skin atrophy or scarring post-involution
searchTerms: skin thinning or scar after lesion heals

rare.symptomName: Functional impairment due to lesion location
rare.notes: E.g. periorbital hemangioma causing visual axis obstruction
searchTerms: loss of function due to lesion site

rare.notes: May lead to cellulitis or abscess formation

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure due to large vascular shunting
rare.notes: Rare but serious complication in very large lesions
searchTerms: heart failure from large blood vessel shunts
cardiac overload due to vascular lesion

laboratory: Possible anemia secondary to ulceration or bleeding
imaging: Ultrasound with Doppler showing high-flow vascular lesion
MRI to assess extent and depth of hemangioma
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations identified
other: Clinical observation of lesion growth pattern
Histopathology if biopsy performed showing proliferating capillaries

distinguishingFeatures: Present at birth and grows proportionally with child

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth causing functional impairment
references: Haggstrom AN, Drolet BA, Baselga E, et al. Prospective study of infantile hemangiomas: clinical characteristics predicting complications and treatment. Pediatrics. 2006;118(3):882-887.
Mulliken JB, Glowacki J. Hemangiomas and vascular malformations in infants and children: a classification based on endothelial characteristics. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1982;69(3):412-422.
